newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher in slow trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended higher against its American counterpart on Saturday, reflecting exporters' continued U.S. dollar sales and local newspapers' projections of a firmer local currency in 1997, dealers said.
The Taiwan dollar finished at T$27.482, back from an intra-session high of T$27.478, against Friday's T$27.487 close.
Turnover through dealers was US$55 million in the shortened Saturday session.

"The Taiwan dollar now faces appreciation pressure as exporters continue to sell their U.S. dollar positions to meet liquidity demand before the Chinese New Year (on February 7)," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"Plus foreign equity funds are expected to continue to flow into Taiwan for the bullish stock market," the dealer said.
A range of T$27.46-50 was seen for next week.
